faq.a: Sami is associated with the Arabic form سَامِي, whose core sense is sami; elevated, lofty.

faq.q: What is the origin of Sami?
faq.a: Sami is associated with Arabic. Sami is Arabic سَامِي (Sāmī), meaning 'elevated, lofty'.
Yes — the underlying form سَامِي is Arabic.
Sami can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sami should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root س م و is Quranic, but Sāmī is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Sami mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Sami is rendered سامی and carries the sense سامی، بلند.

faq.q: What does Sami mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sami is rendered سامی and carries the sense سامی، بلند.
A romanized syllable approximation is sa-mi. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sami?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sami, sami. Script forms are سامي, سامی, سَامِي, सामी.

faq.q: Is Sami a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
